name: MO-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mark Alford running with large financial advantage
Democratic challenger raised only ~$42K with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~5%
model.rationale: The R+21 district, Alford's incumbency, and his roughly 33-to-1 fundraising edge over Jordan Herrera leave no credible path for an upset, and markets agree at about a 5% Democratic chance. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals baseline with no offsetting evidence.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Herrera competitive would be the first sign of movement, but nothing currently suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark Alford seeks a third term in a west-central Missouri district that leans Republican by about 21 points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised nearly $1.4 million and holding about $747,000 on hand, while Democrat Jordan Herrera has raised roughly $42,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Alford about a 96% chance of winning. With the incumbent well-funded in a heavily Republican seat and the challenger lacking resources or outside support, the race is rated Safe Republican with high confidence.
